C2-01-symbiotic-interactions-comparison-chart

A chart with eight small paired-organism panels arranged in two rows, each showing an interaction and its symbols. (1) Root nodules on a groundnut root with tiny bacteria inside, symbols "+ +". (2) An oxpecker bird on a cow's back, "+ +". (3) A remora fish attached under a shark, "+ 0". (4) A tapeworm inside a section of human intestine, "+ −". (5) A hawk catching a chick, "+ −". (6) A Penicillium mould colony with a clear zone in a dish of bacteria, "0 −". (7) A weed and a maize plant with their roots tangled, "− −". (8) An earthworm in soil below a grasshopper on grass, "0 0". Soft greens, blues and browns.
C2-06-predator-prey-population-curves

A line graph of predator and prey numbers over time. Horizontal axis: "time". Vertical axis: "number of organisms". A blue wavy line for prey (higher peaks) and a red wavy line for predators (lower peaks), with each red peak occurring a little after the blue peak before it. Small icons beside the lines: grasshoppers or rats for prey, a hawk or owl for predators. Soft blue and soft red lines.
C2-11-greenhouse-effect-schematic

Diagram of the greenhouse effect. The sun at the top left sends yellow arrows (short-wave sunlight) through a curved band representing the atmosphere down to the Earth's surface (a landscape with fields, a city and factories). Red wavy arrows (infra-red heat) rise from the surface; some escape into space, while others are absorbed by the atmosphere band (dotted with small gas molecules) and bounced back down to the surface. On the ground, small sources of greenhouse gases: a car exhaust, a factory chimney, a gas flare, cattle, a burning forest. Soft yellows, oranges and blues.
C2-12-hydrological-cycle-flow

A water cycle diagram in a Nigerian landscape. Left: the sea with wavy arrows rising (evaporation) to form clouds. Centre: clouds moving inland over hills with rain falling. Right: a forest with arrows rising from the leaves (transpiration), a river flowing back to the sea (run-off), water soaking into the ground and moving downwards to a layer of groundwater, and a well or borehole. A cow drinking at the river and a person sweating, with small arrows showing water vapour. The sun at the top left. Soft blues and greens.
C2-02-symbiotic-mutualism-biological-panels

Three panels showing mutualism. Left: a groundnut plant pulled from the soil showing its roots with many small round pink root nodules, and an enlarged circle showing rod-shaped Rhizobium bacteria inside nodule cells. Middle: a leafy grey-green lichen on a tree trunk, with an enlarged circle of a vertical section showing a layer of green algal cells held among tangled fungal threads. Right: a termite with its hindgut cut open, and an enlarged circle showing a pear-shaped flagellate protozoan covered in many flagella, with small pieces of wood. Trichonympha)", "wood particles". Soft greens, pinks and browns.
C2-03-commensalism-examples

Two panels showing commensalism. Left: underwater scene of a grey shark with a slimmer remora fish attached underneath its body by an oval sucker disc on top of the remora's head, with small scraps of food floating nearby. Right: a savanna scene with a brown and white Nigerian cow grazing and a white cattle egret walking beside its legs, catching a grasshopper that has jumped up from the grass. Soft blues, greens and browns.
C2-04-parasitic-organisms-anatomical-panels

Two panels showing parasites. Left: a tapeworm with its tiny scolex attached to the wall of a cut-open human small intestine, and an enlarged view of the scolex showing a ring of hooks on the rostellum and four round suckers, with a long ribbon of segments trailing behind. Right: a mango tree branch with a bushy Loranthus mistletoe growing on it, with a cut-away section of the branch showing the mistletoe's haustorium penetrating into the host's wood (xylem). The mistletoe has green leaves and small red tubular flowers. Soft pinks, greens and browns.
C2-05-antibiosis-petri-dish

A round Petri dish viewed from above, filled with a pale cream lawn of bacterial growth. In the centre, a blue-green fuzzy Penicillium mould colony, surrounded by a clear circular zone where no bacteria are growing. Soft cream, blue-green and grey.
C2-09-freshwater-pond-food-web

A pond food web drawn over a cross-section of a pond. Surface: floating phytoplankton (shown as tiny green dots), water lettuce, a water lily with a snail on its leaf, mosquito larvae hanging from the surface. Middle water: water fleas, tadpoles, small fish, a dragonfly nymph on a stem. Edge: a frog on the bank and a kingfisher on a branch. Bottom: mud with a catfish and bacteria. Arrows: phytoplankton to water flea, water flea to small fish, small fish to kingfisher, algae to tadpole, tadpole to dragonfly nymph, dragonfly nymph to small fish, algae to mosquito larva, mosquito larva to small fish, small fish to catfish, water lily to snail, mosquito adult to frog. Soft blues and greens.
C2-08-ecological-pyramids-comparison-charts

Three ecological pyramids side by side, each with labelled horizontal bars stacked from bottom to top for producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers and tertiary consumers. (1) Upright pyramid of numbers for grass, grasshoppers, lizards, hawk (wide base, narrow top). (2) Inverted pyramid of numbers for one tree (very narrow base bar with a tree icon), many caterpillars (wide bar), fewer birds (narrower bar) and fewer hawks. (3) Upright pyramid of energy with bars getting about ten times narrower at each level, marked 10,000 kJ, 1,000 kJ, 100 kJ, 10 kJ, and small curved arrows showing heat lost at each level. Soft greens, yellows and oranges.
C2-14-root-nodule-anatomy

Two panels. Left: a cowpea (or groundnut) plant pulled from the soil showing its root system with many small round root nodules. Right: an enlarged cut-away section through one root nodule attached to a root, showing the outer layer, root cells packed with tiny rod-shaped Rhizobium bacteria, a pink-red central zone (leghaemoglobin) and a vascular strand connecting to the root. Arrows show nitrogen gas from soil air entering the nodule, and ammonia/amino acids passing to the plant and sugars passing from the plant to the nodule. Soft greens, browns and pinks.
